grammar.Default rule: si + po; consequent viki po
grammar.Liraasa example: Si maivo po masuma, taivo viki po relsira.
grammar.English meaning: If I had asked, you would have answered.
grammar.Notes / limitations: Canonical if EXISTING; proposed otherwise.

grammar.Default rule: fime/raho/kube/nayo/kasa/kopisa/tuni/sige clauses inherit main clause tense unless locally marked
grammar.Liraasa example: Maivo po sabesia fime taivo lirala.
grammar.Notes / limitations: Canonical if EXISTING; proposed otherwise.

grammar.Default rule: yes/no ki closes clause before vocative
grammar.Liraasa example: Taivo viki pagopa ligo maivo ki, maivo de amor?
grammar.English meaning: Would you come near me, my love?
grammar.Notes / limitations: Canonical if EXISTING; proposed otherwise.

grammar.Default rule: motion prefixes have curated semantic forms only; not automatic for any verb
grammar.Notes / limitations: Canonical if EXISTING; proposed otherwise.

grammar.Default rule: raho precedes dependent relative clause
grammar.Notes / limitations: Canonical if EXISTING; proposed otherwise.

grammar.Default rule: gome before verb; gagu introduces actor
grammar.Liraasa example: Li lira po gome lirala gagu taivo.
grammar.English meaning: The song was sung by you.
grammar.Notes / limitations: Canonical if EXISTING; proposed otherwise.

grammar.Default rule: miyo signals existence; tense may precede
grammar.Notes / limitations: Canonical if EXISTING; proposed otherwise.

grammar.Default rule: loya marks change of state
grammar.Notes / limitations: Canonical if EXISTING; proposed otherwise.

grammar.Default rule: fuyi follows verb; mutual action
grammar.Notes / limitations: Canonical if EXISTING; proposed otherwise.

grammar.Default rule: attach -yo to root, not inflected verb
grammar.Notes / limitations: Canonical if EXISTING; proposed otherwise.

grammar.Default rule: attach -vu to root
grammar.Notes / limitations: Canonical if EXISTING; proposed otherwise.

grammar.Default rule: attach -pago unless root is mavo
grammar.Notes / limitations: Canonical if EXISTING; proposed otherwise.

grammar.Default rule: mavo + pago blocked; mavopago exclusively means society
grammar.Notes / limitations: Canonical if EXISTING; proposed otherwise.

grammar.Default rule: articles, repeated subjects, and ke/ka preceding -san adjective may be omitted with recoverable sense
grammar.Notes / limitations: Canonical if EXISTING; proposed otherwise.

grammar.Default rule: — (unused) means no special lexicalized gloss; compositional literal still available
grammar.Notes / limitations: Canonical if EXISTING; proposed otherwise.

grammar.Default rule: lorejuba informal; lorejuba ala taivo formal
grammar.Notes / limitations: Canonical if EXISTING; proposed otherwise.

grammar.Default rule: evidential directly before the verb (after tense/aspect); certainty marker stays sentence-final
grammar.Liraasa example: Maivo po yehu vimova taivo seye.
grammar.Notes / limitations: Canonical if EXISTING; proposed otherwise.

grammar.Default rule: sacred -asa and -asasan are available for melisma
grammar.Notes / limitations: Canonical if EXISTING; proposed otherwise.

grammar.Default rule: SVO (subject, verb, object); subject/object pronouns stay unchanged.
grammar.Notes / limitations: No person-specific verb conjugations.

grammar.Default rule: Optional articles li / baba; use article before noun.
grammar.Notes / limitations: Use li for known reference and baba for new singular count reference.

grammar.Default rule: Place -san adjective before noun; after copula for predicate.
grammar.Liraasa example: Li vanisan lira. / Li lira ka vanisan.
grammar.English meaning: The beautiful song. / The song is beautiful.
grammar.Notes / limitations: Adjectives do not change for plural or gender.

grammar.Default rule: Attach -ri at the far right of the chosen nominal word form.
grammar.Notes / limitations: Numbers greater than 1 may optionally omit -ri when redundant; preferred default includes -ri.

grammar.Default rule: Attach -ti after the lexical form, and before -ri if plural.
grammar.Notes / limitations: The particle ti is not a separate eighth semantic form.

grammar.Default rule: Owner comes first, de links the possessed noun.
grammar.Notes / limitations: Unlike standard English 'of', order is literally 'you of song'.

grammar.Default rule: Pronoun plus sela.
grammar.Notes / limitations: Avoid inflecting verb stems to express reflexivity.

grammar.Default rule: ke means is/are as a temporary or current state.
grammar.English meaning: The water is cold at the moment.
grammar.Notes / limitations: Not every English 'be' requires the same Dreamsong form.

grammar.Default rule: ka means is/are as an enduring attribute.
grammar.English meaning: The friend is good by nature.
grammar.Notes / limitations: Existing kapoki = previously was; still acceptable.

grammar.Default rule: Simple present unmarked, pressa optional for emphasis.
grammar.Notes / limitations: No English do/does auxiliary.

grammar.Default rule: Place po before verb; does not alter verb stem.
grammar.Notes / limitations: When combined with aspect, tense precedes aspect.

grammar.Default rule: Place futu before verb; future is not identical to hope.
grammar.Notes / limitations: Use kopi only for hope/intention.

grammar.Default rule: roni before main verb.
grammar.Notes / limitations: 'Was singing' = po roni lirala.

grammar.Default rule: tefa before main verb for completed events.
grammar.Notes / limitations: English-perfect mapping is approximate; define finer temporal nuances later.

grammar.Default rule: sahi before verb for a repeated customary action.
grammar.Notes / limitations: Unmarked present remains available.

grammar.Default rule: Modal is placed before verb, after optional tense.
grammar.English meaning: I will be able to sing.
grammar.Notes / limitations: povi can; nosi might; musi must; suvi should; viki would; kopi hope.

grammar.Default rule: ne is immediately before the element negated.
grammar.Notes / limitations: Maivo povi ne lirala = I can choose not to sing (different scope).

grammar.Default rule: -na creates lack/opposite of root concept.
grammar.Notes / limitations: NOT a replacement for ne before sentences.

grammar.Default rule: Verb spellings independent of person, quantity and tense.
grammar.Notes / limitations: Root verbs agree with no person/tense; n/s root verbs end in -nia/-sia, all others repeat initial + a.

grammar.Default rule: Keep SVO and put ki at the end.
grammar.Notes / limitations: No English subject inversion.

grammar.Default rule: Prefix ki- to question concepts, position as English wh-word.
grammar.Notes / limitations: ki-coda what; ki-krono when; ki-nela who (ki-saivo historical); ki-kasa why; ki-modo how.

grammar.Default rule: raho immediately follows the noun being described.
grammar.Liraasa example: Li nela raho lirala ka benasan.
grammar.English meaning: The person who sings is good.
grammar.Notes / limitations: Gap represents the referent; raho works for who/which/that.

grammar.Default rule: si introduces the condition; result follows comma.
grammar.Notes / limitations: No special conditional verb inflection.

grammar.Default rule: sina introduces a negative condition.
grammar.Liraasa example: Sina saivo pagopa, maivo ne lirala.
grammar.English meaning: Unless they go, I do not sing.
grammar.Notes / limitations: Can be replaced with si ... ne for transparency.

grammar.Default rule: kasa links effect to its reason.
grammar.Liraasa example: Maivo somusia kasa maivo ke silisan.
grammar.English meaning: I sleep because I am cold.
grammar.Notes / limitations: Original function word kept.

grammar.Default rule: kopisa links action and intended consequence.
grammar.English meaning: I work in order to do good.
grammar.Notes / limitations: Subjects may repeat; omission optional only if unambiguous.

grammar.Default rule: kasi/menu before adjective; tamo before comparison target.
grammar.Liraasa example: Li lira ka kasi vanisan tamo li seno.
grammar.English meaning: The song is more beautiful than the speech.
grammar.Notes / limitations: mosa/lusu express ordinary most/least, not ascended -asasan.

grammar.Default rule: la + adjective, usually after verb/object or preceding predicate.
grammar.Notes / limitations: -san means adjective even where the original spreadsheet glossed an adverb.

grammar.Default rule: Use ata, oro, nara between parallel clauses or nouns.
grammar.Notes / limitations: Conjunctions don't need seven lexical forms.

grammar.Default rule: First root modifies second; compound's right edge supplies semantic head.
grammar.Notes / limitations: Historical compounds may be lexicalized exceptions.

grammar.Default rule: Treat established compounds as roots and add derivations to whole.
grammar.Notes / limitations: Preserves original lexicon pattern.

grammar.Default rule: -asa/-asasan = transcendent state; mosa = high ordinary degree.
grammar.Notes / limitations: Ascension not just 'the most'.

grammar.Default rule: Sacred, formal and ordinary wording use same basic grammar.
grammar.Notes / limitations: Maivo formerly labeled divine/formal; decide later whether to create an everyday I.

grammar.Default rule: Numeral before count noun; plural noun optional but preferred for >1.
grammar.Notes / limitations: No grammatical number gender agreement.

grammar.Default rule: Color roots precede nouns; hue + qualifier compounds are adjectives by use.
grammar.Notes / limitations: Full color matrix maintained in Colors.

grammar.Default rule: fime introduces content clause; raho remains relative
grammar.Notes / limitations: PROPOSAL | No comma needed before fime; not a question and not a relative pronoun.

grammar.Default rule: sidu introduces infinitive-like bare verb; subject shared
grammar.Notes / limitations: PROPOSAL | Conjugation remains only lexical; infinitive has the same derived stem.

grammar.Default rule: kube introduces a time adjunct clause; ki-krono only questions
grammar.Notes / limitations: PROPOSAL | If either event is in past/future, mark time at its own verb.

grammar.Default rule: nayo introduces overlap
grammar.Notes / limitations: PROPOSAL | Scope includes its whole following clause.

grammar.Default rule: tuni introduces end-point event
grammar.Notes / limitations: PROPOSAL | Future not entailed; both clauses can be explicitly tensed.

grammar.Default rule: sige anchors starting point in time (not because)
grammar.Liraasa example: Sige maivo po venreva, taivo lirala.
grammar.Notes / limitations: PROPOSAL | Reason uses kasa; tense since uses sige.

grammar.Default rule: kureli signals minimal delay after subevent
grammar.English meaning: As soon as you come, I sing.
grammar.Notes / limitations: PROPOSAL | If chronology matters add tense particles independently.

grammar.Default rule: Drop second-person subject; start with bare verb
grammar.Notes / limitations: PROPOSAL | Addressed to listener; mood by subject-drop and punctuation.

grammar.Default rule: ne + plain verb; second-person subject dropped
grammar.Notes / limitations: PROPOSAL | Not negated root suffix -na.

grammar.Default rule: yava + verb = let us; first plural subject implicit
grammar.Notes / limitations: PROPOSAL | Includes speaker; optional explicit maivori is avoided.

grammar.Default rule: Approved productive causative: vaku introduces a causer before actor/patient and the base verb.
grammar.English meaning: I kill the person [cause them to die].
grammar.Notes / limitations: APPROVED | Plain bioba = live, daigoda = die, tranata = change; use vaku for cause to live / kill / cause to change.

grammar.Default rule: gome before transitive verb, optional by-agent gagu
grammar.Liraasa example: Li dorbi gome sevresia gagu li sora.
grammar.English meaning: The door is closed by the friend.
grammar.Notes / limitations: PROPOSAL | Intransitives cannot form a passive without a transitive lexical reading.

grammar.Default rule: miyo impersonal; no expletive noun/pronoun
grammar.Notes / limitations: PROPOSAL | One invariant miyo for singular/plural.

grammar.Default rule: loya is change-of-state copula (ke/ka static)
grammar.Notes / limitations: PROPOSAL | Changes state without identifying causer; use vaku for cause.

grammar.Default rule: fuyi replaces shared object in symmetric event
grammar.Notes / limitations: PROPOSAL | Use only with two or more participants.

grammar.Default rule: ki-eli introduces choice from known set
grammar.Notes / limitations: PROPOSAL | ki-coda = what; ki-eli asks selection.

grammar.Default rule: ki-nela is preferred human question; ki-saivo historical
grammar.Notes / limitations: PROPOSAL | Keep historical form accepted, not preferred.

grammar.Default rule: Root + -yo makes an agent noun (singer, teacher), NOT verb stem + -yo.
grammar.Notes / limitations: PROPOSAL | 10 productive examples appear in Examples sheet.

grammar.Default rule: Root + -pago denotes place of activity; blocked on mavo; the compound mavopago exclusively means society.
grammar.Notes / limitations: PROPOSAL | Literal structural place meaning; not every word has a conventional place.

grammar.Default rule: Root + -vu is ordinary grandness, not divine -asa.
grammar.Notes / limitations: PROPOSAL | -ti small; -vu large; -asa mythic/qualitative.

grammar.Default rule: Time/place correlative compounds replace standalone adverb roots.
grammar.Notes / limitations: PROPOSAL | New 0.3 temporals may be free adverbials, without separate particle.

grammar.Default rule: Everyday Lorejuba!; formal Lorejuba ala taivo!; thank (verb) jurevija.
grammar.Pattern / placement: lorejuba ala PERSON / S + jurevija + PERSON
grammar.Notes / limitations: APPROVED | lorejuba ala taivo is the standard expression of thanks; grasia was retired from the active vocabulary.

grammar.Default rule: One preverb after time/modal/aspect and before lexical V: yehu/gesu/bisu/vuda/buyu
grammar.Notes / limitations: PROPOSAL | Only one primary evidential per proposition; yehu seen, gesu heard, bisu felt, vuda dreamed, buyu reported.

grammar.Default rule: Final seye/mufe/poye/pifu, after object or other complements
grammar.Notes / limitations: PROPOSAL | seye sure; mufe likely; poye perhaps; pifu wish/hope. Not required in every sentence.

grammar.Default rule: maivo is the ONLY first-person form; no everyday alternative.
grammar.Notes / limitations: APPROVED | maivo + de indicates possession; maivo and maivo use unchanged English-like subject/object order.

grammar.Default rule: In poetry only, omit li/baba; omit a repeated known subject; or omit ke/ka before -san adjective.
grammar.Liraasa example: Li nela ke vanisan. → Nela vanisan.
grammar.Notes / limitations: Never elide arguments if ambiguity would result.

grammar.Default rule: The definite article li before a -san form yields a substantive: the one who is X.
grammar.Notes / limitations: No silent additional noun; contextual gender-neutral reading.

grammar.Default rule: Natural weather event verbs can appear with no dummy pronoun it.
grammar.Notes / limitations: Use lexical rain/snow root; subjectless only for impersonal phenomena.

grammar.Default rule: Capitalized proper name is an uninflected noun. Vocative takes a comma, no special particle.
grammar.Notes / limitations: Names should not be mistaken for root-derived forms.

grammar.Default rule: Add -ne to an uninflected cardinal string; first una-ne, second dossa-ne.
grammar.Notes / limitations: Not a seven-form suffix; usable with compound cardinal readings.

grammar.Default rule: Fraction = numerator de denominator, optionally followed by noun. Half lexicalized as una-de-dossa.
grammar.Notes / limitations: No rounding implied; de functions as mathematical of.

grammar.Default rule: Correlative nuna-krono is a full emphatic never; avoid stacking sentential ne unless needed to disambiguate.
grammar.Notes / limitations: This replaces the older never root nuna-krono.

grammar.Default rule: Invariable existential word is defined and exemplified consistently in lowercase.
grammar.Notes / limitations: If miyo is respelled, all examples use its current particle form.

grammar.Default rule: mavo + pago never creates the productive place noun; mavopago is lexicalized society.
grammar.Notes / limitations: Formal homophony is prohibited in productive derivation.

grammar.Default rule: Agentive attaches to the ROOT, not the derived verb.
grammar.Notes / limitations: Root-based; avoids -ri plural homography.

grammar.Default rule: Large, grand, extensive; ordinary magnitude (not sacred ascension).
grammar.Notes / limitations: -vu is independent of poetic -asa.

grammar.Default rule: Place associated with activity/concept, except blocked mavo.
grammar.Notes / limitations: Right-headed lexicalized compounds can override literal readings.

grammar.Default rule: A speaker-source marker precedes main verb after tense/modal/aspect; only one primary source marker.
grammar.Notes / limitations: Five author-approved speaker knowledge sources; see Function Words.

grammar.Default rule: Sentence-final certainty marker comes after predicate and its complements.
grammar.Notes / limitations: Four author-approved endings; see Function Words.

grammar.Default rule: Lorejuba! everyday; Lorejuba ala taivo! formal and addressed.
grammar.English meaning: Thank you. / Thank you very much.
grammar.Notes / limitations: jurevija is the separate finite verb to thank. Historical grasia is not active.

discourse_particles.register: everyday (also poetic for hesitant speech; not sacred)
discourse_particles.notes: May be lengthened in performance (spelling never changes) and repeated (hema, hema). Never ends a clause before ki.

examples.liraasa: Taivo futu relnura ki? — Hema. Poye.
examples.english: Will you come back? — Well. Maybe.

examples.liraasa: Maivo vurlova, hema, baba cupa de miru.
examples.english: I'd like, um, a cup of water.

examples.liraasa: Hema, hema… li bumre ne keleka.
examples.english: Well, well… the bread isn't rising.

discourse_particles.function: self-repair: cancels the speaker's own preceding word, phrase or clause and replaces it ("I mean", "rather", "no —")
discourse_particles.positions: immediately after the abandoned item and before its replacement; or clause-initial to reformulate a whole previous utterance
discourse_particles.notes: Contrast with corrective negation ne X, nara Y, which corrects a proposition (often someone else's); nido corrects the speaker's own wording. Content before nido is withdrawn.

examples.liraasa: Maivo po bumreba tressa, nido, cuara bumreri.
examples.english: I baked three, I mean, four loaves.

examples.liraasa: Taivo ka benasan. Nido, taivo ka ruli benasan.
examples.english: You're good. I mean, you're very good.

examples.liraasa: Maivo amora taivo, nido, maivo devoda taivo.
examples.english: I love you, no, I pledge myself to you.

examples.liraasa: Maivo po bumreba ne tressa, nara cuara bumreri.
examples.english: I baked not three but four loaves. (corrective negation, for contrast)

discourse_particles.function: topic return / closure ("anyway", "at any rate"); with a possessive seno phrase, resumption ("as I was saying")
discourse_particles.notes: Yori, maivo de seno = as I was saying. Yori, taivo de seno = back to what you were saying. Standalone Yori. is dismissive.

examples.liraasa: Yori, maivo de seno: li bumrepago nedunia cono.
examples.english: As I was saying: the bakery needs coins.

examples.liraasa: Yori, taivo de seno. Taivo po senosia fime pilo po lenila maivo.
examples.english: Back to what you were saying. You said father heard me.

discourse_particles.function: irony / sarcasm: the speaker does not endorse, or mocks, the proposition
discourse_particles.positions: clause-final, in the attitude slot (instead of seye/mufe/poye/pifu); may precede ki; standalone
discourse_particles.notes: Cannot co-occur with a certainty marker. Using zoke after sacred vocabulary is irreverent but does not change the sacred word's canonical meaning.

grammar_rulings_0_8.ruling: The JSON is authoritative; the workbook is generated. Language field and files are named Liraasa.
An unused form may receive a gloss only when its compositional meaning is predictable, approved case by case, and recorded in authorized_changes.
Frozen for 0.8. No canonical root is respelled; the 40-root queue carries forward unchanged.

A standalone tense particle opening a paragraph or turn (Po — / Futu —) sets a frame: following unmarked main clauses take that tense until another tense particle, pressa, or the end of the paragraph. Optional. Time words do not set a frame, so 0.7 texts keep their meaning.
li may be omitted in everyday speech as well as verse when the referent is obvious; never when ambiguous. baba may be omitted only in verse.
sige clauses never inherit tense; they are always marked. Tense inheritance applies to fime, raho, kube, nayo, kasa, kopisa and tuni.
deyaapo is kept as a fossil (it retains the retired past marker apo). apo is not used in new compounds; say vesno de deyaapo.
amorliraa, amorrinbaa and amorvulraa are correct; each a is its own syllable.
A certainty marker (or zoke) precedes ki: Taivo lirala poye ki?
Registers are defined in the grammar guide. The lexicon keeps everyday and poetic labels; sacred is added only to headwords whose root meaning is inherently sacred, after review.
New vocabulary is sized by genuine gaps, not by the 120-150 target.
The diminutive -ti may attach to personal names as an affectionate or teasing form (Dorinti).

eli/ola (and eliri/olari) stand alone for things, situations and discourse (ola = what was just said; eli = what follows). For people use eli-nela/ola-nela or saivo, except presentational Eli ka NAME.

ne precedes what it negates: verb or modal (after tense), copula (ne ka), noun phrase or fragment (Ne eli), or a contrasted constituent (ne X, nara Y). Negation is compositional: ne + nuna- is a positive (avoid).

Everyday speech may omit a repeated subject in coordinated clauses and in answers, omit a repeated predicate after a contrasting subject (Dorin, ne.), answer with tense + verb (Po sapusia.), and echo a word with ki. Speech may break off after any particle; the listener may complete it.

ki may close the main clause before an appended direct quotation (Taivo vurlova ki, fime maivo senosia: "...") as well as after it (0.7 order). Embedded wh-questions keep the wh-word in place with no ki; embedded yes/no questions use si (whether).
Inside an inheriting clause: tefa marks prior action, nayo/roni simultaneous, futu subsequent (future-in-past), sahi habitual.

The root (form 1) is the noun of action or thing (juba, donu, tali). A verb phrase becomes a noun phrase with sidu (Sidu lisrola ka livna de taivo) or a clause with fime (Fime taivo po relnura ka baba juba).
[toda|rada|muya|poka|somi|nuna] [li|eli|ola|OWNER de] [NUMBER] [ADJ...] NOUN[-ti][-ri] [de ...] [raho ...]. toda N = every N; toda li N = all the N; toda OWNER de N = all OWNER's N.
X ka sambasan ko Y (same as); X ka sambanasan da Y (different from); gase NP alone = like NP (simile); gase ADJ gase NP = as ADJ as NP. Lotero silda, ... = on the other hand.
